blocks.text: Imagine an ash tree whose branches spread across the whole world [1]. Yggdrasil, the Norse world tree, stands at the centre of the universe [2]. The Nine Worlds surround Yggdrasil, making the tree a way to picture how the Norse universe fits together [3]. A squirrel carries an eagle’s words down the tree, while a dragon gnaws at the roots below [4][5].

blocks.caption: The Course’s own illustration shows Yggdrasil with nine surrounding worlds and creatures above and below.
blocks.alt: A spreading ash tree labelled Yggdrasil stands among nine softly outlined areas labelled collectively Nine Worlds. Three main roots extend below it. An eagle sits above a squirrel on the trunk, and a dragon gnaws a root beneath the tree.

sections.heading: Worlds for gods, humans, and the dead

blocks.text: Asgard is a realm, or world, of the gods [5]. Midgard is the realm of humans [2]. A rainbow bridge joins Asgard and Midgard [2]. Hel is a realm of the dead, initially associated with those who died of illness or old age [2]. The sources leave uncertainty about exactly who goes to Hel [2].

A poem places Hel beneath one root, giants beneath another, and humans beneath the third [4]. Another account places one root among the gods, another among giants, and the third above a world of ice and mist [1][2]. Yggdrasil connects the Nine Worlds, but the sources give its roots different settings [2][4][1].
